questions.title: Perimeters of similar triangles
questions.text: The perimeters of two similar triangles are 56 cm and 70 cm respectively. If one side of the first triangle is 14 cm, then the corresponding side of the second triangle (in cm) is:
steps: ① Similar ⟹ every side is scaled by the same factor
② So the perimeters scale by that factor too
questions.remember: Similar triangles: ratio of perimeters = ratio of corresponding sides.
questions.trap: Writing 14/x = 70/56 and getting 11.2. Keep first triangle over second on BOTH sides.
questions.tryit: Perimeters of two similar triangles are 30 cm and 20 cm. One side of the first is 12 cm. Find the corresponding side of the second.

questions.title: DE ∥ AB: find x in terms of a, b, c
questions.text: In ΔABC, DE || AB. If AB = a, DE = x, BE = b and EC = c. Then x expressed in terms of a, b and c is ______.
steps: ① DE ∥ AB cuts off a small △CED
⑤ DE/AB = CE/CB, and CB = b + c
questions.remember: A line parallel to one side cuts off a small triangle SIMILAR to the whole triangle.
questions.trap: Using CE/EB = c/b. For DE/AB you need the WHOLE side: CE/CB = c/(b + c).
questions.tryit: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm and BC = 10 cm. Find DE.

questions.title: AE/EB = AF/FC = 1/2: compare EF and BC
questions.text: E and F are points on the sides AB and AC, respectively, of a ΔABC, such that AE/EB = AF/FC = 1/2. Which of the following relations is true?
steps: ② Converse of BPT ⟹ EF ∥ BC
④ AE = 1 part, EB = 2 parts ⟹ AB = 3 parts
questions.remember: Converse of BPT: if a line divides two sides in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
questions.trap: Taking EF/BC = 1/2. The side ratio is AE/AB = 1/3, not AE/EB.

questions.title: 2AB = DE: find EF
questions.text: If ∆ ABC and ∆ DEF are similar such that 2AB = DE and BC = 8 cm, then EF = ______.
questions.remember: Order of letters = order of matching: △ABC ~ △DEF means AB ↔ DE, BC ↔ EF, CA ↔ FD.
questions.trap: Reading 2AB = DE as AB = 2DE and picking 4 cm.
questions.tryit: △PQR ~ △XYZ, 3PQ = XY and QR = 5 cm. Find YZ.

questions.title: ∠PQR = ∠QSP: find PR
questions.text: In the given figure, if ∠PQR = ∠QSP, PQ = 6 cm and PS = 3 cm, then find the length of PR.
steps: ⑤ PQ/PS = PR/PQ ⟹ PQ² = PS × PR
questions.remember:
Write similar triangles in MATCHING order: equal angles in the same positions.
△PQR ~ △PSQ ⟹ PQ/PS = QR/SQ = PR/PQ
questions.trap: Writing △PQR ~ △PQS (wrong order) and then pairing the wrong sides.
questions.tryit: D is on BC of △ABC with ∠ADC = ∠BAC. If CA = 6 cm and CB = 9 cm, find CD.

questions.title: Parallelogram: prove △ABE ~ △CFB
questions.text: In the parallelogram ABCD, side AD is produced at point E, and BE intersects CD at point F. Prove that ΔABE ∼ ΔCFB.
steps: ① Given: ABCD is a ∥gm, E on AD produced
④ AE ∥ BC, and BE cuts across both
questions.remember: In a parallelogram: opposite angles are equal, and opposite sides are parallel, so look for ALTERNATE angles.
questions.trap: Writing 'similar by AA' without giving a reason for each angle. Each reason carries marks.
questions.tryit: In the same figure, AB = 6 cm, BC = 4 cm and AE = 9 cm. Find CF.

questions.title: BPT: statement, proof and trapezium application
questions.text:
Prove that a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, divides the other two sides in the same ratio.
Using the above theorem solve the following: PQRS is a trapezium with PQ ‖ SR. X and Y are points on non-parallel sides PS and QR respectively such that XY ‖ PQ. Show that PX/XS = QY/YR.
steps: ① Given: △ABC, DE ∥ BC · To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC
② Constr: join BE, CD; draw EN ⊥ AB, DM ⊥ AC
⑤ ar(BDE) = ar(DEC) (same base DE, DE ∥ BC)
⑦ Trapezium: join PR, it meets XY at M
questions.remember: BPT proof in 3 moves: same HEIGHT ⟹ area ratio = base ratio (twice), then same BASE and same PARALLELS ⟹ equal areas.
questions.trap: Skipping the construction or the reason 'same base, between the same parallels'. Both carry marks.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 6 · Theorem 6.1 · Exercise 6.2 (Q2, Q10 types)
questions.tryit: ABCD is a trapezium, AB ∥ DC, and its diagonals meet at O. Show that AO/BO = CO/DO.
questions.tryans: Draw EO ∥ DC through O; use BPT in △ADC and △ABD

questions.title: Case study: the triangle cabinet
questions.text:
Triangle is a very popular shape used in interior designing. A cabinet's largest triangle is ΔABC and the smallest one, with a shelf, is ΔDEF. PQ is parallel to EF.
(i) Show that ΔDPQ ∼ ΔDEF.  (ii) If DP = 50 cm and PE = 70 cm, find PQ/EF.  (iii) If 2AB = 5DE and ΔABC ∼ ΔDEF, show that (perimeter of ΔABC)/(perimeter of ΔDEF) is constant. [OR: If AM and DN are medians of ΔABC and ΔDEF, prove that ΔABM ∼ ΔDEN.]
questions.remember:
Similar triangles: ratio of perimeters = ratio of corresponding sides.
Medians of similar triangles split matching sides in half, so BM/EN = BC/EF.
questions.trap: Taking PQ/EF = DP/PE = 50/70. Compare with the WHOLE side DE = 120 cm.
questions.tryit: If DP = 30 cm and PE = 45 cm, find PQ/EF.
